A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same floating-point quantization scaling-law study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original language-model training experiments, quantization ablations, fitted scaling laws, and held-out validation using 1.2B-parameter models.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and additionally reports validation results for 7B- and 70B-parameter models in Figure 4.

M1.justification: The quantization procedure, P2/P4/P6 targets, and proposed scaling-law formula remain unchanged. Naming the law Capybara and explaining the choice of exponent and mantissa inputs do not introduce a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions study language-model pretraining and validation on the same Dolma V1.7 subset with the stated OLMo sampling proportions. The added larger models change experimental configurations, not dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparisons retain the Kumar precision scaling law and the Chinchilla/OpenAI classical scaling laws. The new discussion of Kuzmin et al. and SQNR does not report an evaluated additional comparator.

E3.justification: Held-out evaluation expands substantially in model scale, from 1.2B to include 7B and 70B models. Table 3 adds E4M3, block-size-64 configurations at approximately 10/100B tokens for 7B and 10/20B tokens for 70B. Existing configurations and fitting membership remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing test of extrapolation beyond the fitted model sizes gains larger-model validation in v2 Figure 4. The quantization-target, exponent/mantissa, and scaling-factor analyses remain unchanged; their consolidation in Appendix B does not constitute new analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed-based replication, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The stated runs concern configuration sweeps; the additional validation configurations do not introduce a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 Figure 4 adds actual-versus-predicted loss results for the four larger-model configurations absent from v1 Figure 14. These are additional validation results, not same-setting performance gains. Table 2's fitted constants and the existing experimental findings are retained.

T1.justification: The scaling-law mathematics and derivations for optimal bit allocation, effective parameters, critical data size, and compute optimality remain substantively unchanged. v1 Appendices A–C become v2 Appendices C–E; equation consolidation and precision notation changes do not alter the reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the unified scaling law, exponent–mantissa allocation, critical data size, and a compute-optimal precision range of 4–8 bits. Capybara is a new name, and larger-model validation supports existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 adds a substantive modeling rationale: SQNR can account for distribution transformations but depends on tensor distributions, motivating direct use of exponent and mantissa bits. The existing interpretations of overtraining, knowledge intensity, and compute optimality remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies architecture details and configurations for the new 7B/70B experiments, adds a 10% decay-rate entry to Table 1, and identifies the target-quantization experiment as FP3. The latter disclosures do not establish changes to the previously conducted experiments.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kuzmin et al. (2022), 'FP8 Quantization: The Power of the Exponent,' and discusses SQNR as an alternative modeling basis. Other reference changes largely update publication metadata for existing works; the overall research positioning remains.

P1.justification: v2 substantially condenses and reorganizes the exposition, replaces numerous numbered subsections with paragraph headings, and creates appendices for hyperparameters and fitting details. It also introduces Capybara terminology and naming explanation, plus acknowledgements and an impact statement.

P2.justification: Figures are extensively merged, resized, and relocated. v2 Figure 1 juxtaposes selected existing baseline/proposed-law panels; Figure 2 combines the target diagram and ablation plot; many fitting plots and Tables 1–2 move to appendices. Figure 4 adds validation series. The running header incorrectly becomes the ICML template title.

improvement.justification: Validation at 7B and 70B adds useful evidence beyond v1's 1.2B checks, supported by documented configurations. The SQNR rationale and consolidated comparisons also improve explanation. The gain is limited because the new large-model tests cover only E4M3 with block size 64; smaller plots and the erroneous template header reduce presentation quality.
